sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
hindiTranslation: हे महाबाहो  जो मनुष्य न किसीसे द्वेष करता है और न किसीकी आकाङ्क्षा करता है वह कर्मयोगी सदा संन्यासी समझनेयोग्य है क्योंकि द्वन्द्वोंसे रहित मनुष्य सुखपूर्वक संसारबन्धनसे मुक्त हो जाता है ॥
englishTranslation: One who neither hates nor desires is always a renunciant. Free from opposites, such a person is easily released from bondage, O mighty-armed one.
essence: Freedom comes when craving and resistance no longer steer the mind.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: A true renunciant is not someone who abandons action, but someone who drops hatred and craving. Freedom comes when inner opposites no longer pull the mind.
simpleInsight: Drop hatred and craving, and you have renounced enough to be free.
detailedMeaning: Krishna now sharpens the teaching. Real renunciation means inner freedom from hatred, craving, and the tug of opposites, whatever one's outward life.
modernRelevance: A widower keeps his house and his job, yet stops resenting his brother over the old land case and stops wanting the plot back. Krishna would call him a renunciant already, since hatred and craving have loosened their grip.
translationLiteral: ज्ञेयः (to be understood) / सः (that one) / नित्यसंन्यासी (always-renunciant) / यः (who) / न (not) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / न (not) / काङ्क्षति (desires) / निर्द्वन्द्वः (free from opposites) / हि (indeed) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / सुखम् (easily) / बन्धात् (from bondage) / प्रमुच्यते (is released)
insight: Krishna defines the true renunciant as one who neither hates nor craves, whatever outward life they lead.

quoteVariants.text: Neither hate nor craving binds you. Freedom begins there.
What binds me most is wanting and resisting.
Release hate, release craving, live free.
